newsitem.title: CHINA: China and Taiwan confirm Hong Kong shipping pact.
newsitem.headline: China and Taiwan confirm Hong Kong shipping pact.

text.p: China said on Monday it had confirmed an agreement reached last month with arch-rival Taipei that allows Taiwan and Hong Kong ships to visit each other's ports after the British colony returns to Chinese rule.

China's Association for Relations Across the Taiwan Straits and its quasi-official Taiwan counterpart, the Straits Exchange Foundation, had exchanged letters confirming a memorandum on links signed on May 24, the official Xinhua news agency said.

The association's letter said it agreed with the stipulations of the memorandum, which will allow shipping links to continue after 156 years of colonial rule in Hong Kong end at midnight on June 30, Xinhua said.
Most forms of direct shipping links between communist China and its Nationalist-ruled island rival Taiwan are banned.

Under the May pact, Hong Kong-registered ships would fly the flag of the post-colonial Hong Kong Special Administrative Region on their stern flagpoles and no flag on their masts during the time between entering and leaving Taiwan ports, Xinhua said.
Between entering and leaving Hong Kong's ports, Taiwan-registered commercial vessels would fly no flag on either mast or flagpole, it said.
Vessels registered in either the mainland or Taiwan could fly their company flags and signal flags, it said.
Both sides have described the flags agreement as temporary, but have given no indication of a timetable for revising it.
